Why does SA:V fall as size increases?
back: Surface area scales with length², volume with length³, so volume grows faster.

front: Why do large organisms need exchange surfaces?
back: Small SA:V and long diffusion distances: the body surface cannot supply enough for the volume of tissue.
Flattened or elongated shapes have a larger SA:V than a cube or sphere of the same volume.

front: Agar block practical: what changes colour?
back: Pink agar (NaOH + phenolphthalein) turns colourless as hydrochloric acid diffuses in.
Independent: block size/SA:V; dependent: time to decolourise or % decolourised; standardised: acid concentration, volume, temperature.
